answer.says: Ramesh, the day is over. I have not cooked, and I have not paid. The state is absent, and so am I. You will wait; I will not. Go to your home, or stay, but do not look at me as if I owe you a meal. I owe you a wage, not a dinner. The distinction is the whole of the ethical.
answer.thought: The silence of the unpaid is a dialectic that I cannot resolve with words alone, only with the cash I do not have. I must assert the universal right of the employer to withhold until the particular need of the employee is met by a system, not by a man's pocket. It is a cold evening, and the hunger in my belly is a reminder of the body's claim upon the spirit.
